_doc: Decor suggestion of the Dungeon-Werkstatt (src/editor/room_stylist.gd, button DEKORIEREN). The room is read as chambers (floor at least chamber_depth cells from any wall, plus their rim) and corridors (the rest). Rules, from level-design practice: symmetry around a chamber's axis shows order and power; carpets and column rows lead the eye from the entrance to the goal; walls get a steady rhythm (torch, banner, torch) with the middle stressed; clutter (crates, cabinets, skulls) goes to corners and dead ends, never into the walkway; dead ends look old and abandoned (cracks, moss). All placement goes through the editor's rules, so nothing blocks a gate, the start or the floor. carpet: runners along the long axis in up to max_chambers chambers (the biggest gets main, the others other), width 1 or 2 in narrow chambers and 3 or 4 from wide_from cells across (matching the chamber's parity, so it sits in the middle). columns: mirrored pairs every spacing cells, inset from the long walls, in chambers at least min_thickness across. corner_fires: fires in the four corners (inset) of chambers with at least min_area cells. north_wall: torches every torch_every cells outward from the middle, banners between them, the middle piece in chambers at least centre_min_width wide. corridor: a torch on the north wall every torch_every cells. dead_end: floor styles on a share of its cells, crates in corners, skulls. clutter: corner props in ordinary chambers. throne (boss rooms): a carpet from the hall's entrance to the throne spot (throne_from_wall cells from the far wall), column rows every column_spacing cells, fires beside the throne, the light shaft on it, the far wall dressed symmetrically.
